claims.name: The Heil Co.
claims.quote: Between February and March 2026, The Heil Co. removed and inspected CNG cylinders from fourteen (14) customer vehicles equipped with the same ladder configuration.

cause.quote: An incorrect length bolt may be installed during initial build or during ladder service.

upstream.quote: Measurements of the observed blemishes were evaluated against the cylinder manufacturer's damage assessment criteria and were determined to be within repairable limits.

events.quote: In November 2025 Heil learned that a ladder mounting bracket may have been assembled with a bolt longer than specified in one leg of the ladder support structure on a customer unit.
however, The Heil Co. initiated an investigation to evaluate the potential for cylinder-to-bolt contact.
Between February and March 2026, The Heil Co. removed and inspected CNG cylinders from fourteen (14) customer vehicles equipped with the same ladder configuration.
Inspection identified surface blemishes on seven (7) cylinders in an area corresponding to the location of the ladder mounting bolt.
Measurements of the observed blemishes were evaluated against the cylinder manufacturer's damage assessment criteria and were determined to be within repairable limits.
The Heil Co. continued its investigation to determine the mechanism by which the observed blemishes could occur.

The investigation determined that installation of an incorrect bolt at one particular location during vehicle assembly or during subsequent service and inspection activities could reduce the intended clearance between the ladder structure and the cylinder.
The investigation continued through July and early August 2026.

Based on the investigation findings, The Heil Co. concluded that an incorrect bolt could potentially be installed in the affected location and could reduce the designed clearance to the adjacent CNG cylinder,
To eliminate the possibility of incorrect bolt installation at this location, The Heil Co. implemented a design change on August 4, 2026, removing the ladder support leg containing the subject bolt .
On August 11, 2026, The Heil Co. determined that the condition described above constituted a safety- related defect and decided to conduct a voluntary safety recall.

claims.name: Ford
claims.quote: On March 5, 2026, Ford’s Critical Concern Review Group (CCRG) opened an investigation into loose or missing rear Panhard rod fasteners on 2026 MY Ford F-150 Raptor vehicles.

cause.quote: The error-proofing device at the relevant torque station was in bypass mode for a period during production, resulting in incomplete or non-conforming torque data for some vehicles.

events.quote: On February 23, 2026, Dearborn Truck Plant (DTP) was alerted to a warranty claim on a model year (MY) 2026 Ford F-150 Raptor regarding a “customer rattle.”
Upon further inspection, the dealer confirmed that the rear Panhard rod was loose.
Further Investigation by DTP concluded that the error- proofing data for the relevant torque station was in bypass mode from December 27, 2025, until January 23, 2026.
A review of the torque data confirmed the vehicles that either did not meet the torque requirement or had missing/incomplete rundown data.
On March 5, 2026, Ford’s Critical Concern Review Group (CCRG) opened an investigation into loose or missing rear Panhard rod fasteners on 2026 MY Ford F-150 Raptor vehicles.
As part of its ongoing investigation, CCRG evaluated the geometry of the suspension system and detectability of a loose Panhard rod.
CCRG continued its evaluation and in August 2026 ultimately determined that the loose condition may not be detectable from inside the cabin.
CCRG also considered the likely usage of these vehicles by owners, many of whom are driving or racing enthusiasts.

In August 2026, Ford's Global Data Insight and Analytics (GDIA) team completed a statistical analysis of the potentially affected population, which indicated a low likelihood of future field failures.
On September 1, 2026, Ford’s Field Review Committee reviewed the concern and approved a field service action.

cause.quote: Affected brake hoses might not meet durability specifications as a result of accumulated material fatigue due to increased thermal and mechanical stresses sustained over the vehicle’s lifetime.

events.quote: This recall expands upon the vehicle population subject to Recall No. 25V116, filed on February 24, 2025.
Based on the field information and technical evidence then available, MBAG had identified two factors associated with the condition: climatic exposure and a particular vehicle production period.
MBAG therefore defined the original recall population using those factors.
Following the decision to conduct a recall, MBAG continued monitoring field performance of the front brake hoses, including vehicles both within and outside the original recall population.
Between March and August 2025, MBAG received additional field reports from markets outside the United States involving vehicles produced outside the original recall production range

These reports presented information that was not reflected in the data available when the original recall population was determined and prompted MBAG to reassess whether the condition might extend beyond the originally identified production period and climatic regions.

During September and October 2025, MBAG reviewed the additional reports and available vehicle and production information to determine the appropriate means of obtaining and analyzing representative field parts.
In November 2025, MBAG began coordinating a dedicated Field Engineering Activity to obtain additional brake hoses from vehicles exhibiting the reported condition.
From November 2025 through February 2026, MBAG identified candidate vehicles and markets, developed the collection protocol, and coordinated the retrieval and shipment of the requested components.
The Field Engineering Activity was formally launched in March 2026.
By June 2026, the requested brake hose components had been collected and returned to MBAG.
MBAG forwarded the components to the supplier for detailed technical analysis and testing.
In July 2026, MBAG reviewed and discussed the results of the supplier’s laboratory and durability testing for the retrieved field parts.

Based on the additional field reports, the analysis of the retrieved components, and the resulting laboratory and durability testing, MBAG reassessed the affected vehicle population with respect to production range and climatic restrictions.
As a result, MBAG identified an expanded vehicle scope covering vehicles produced up to the implementation of a modified brake hose design in series production.
MBAG subsequently identified the potentially affected vehicles in the field.
On September 25, 2026, MBAG determined that a potential safety risk cannot be ruled out for the expanded vehicle population and decided to expand the recall.
